findings.title: Rust semantic-universe keyComponents are necessary but not sufficient
findings.detail: Listed: provider/version, toolchain identity, config roots, edition/target, feature/conditional-compilation selection, execution-capable flag. Missing for real Cargo/rustc soundness: (1) full cfg set beyond features (target_os/arch/env, debug_assertions, test, custom --cfg); (2) package set / Cargo.lock / dependency feature unification; (3) RUSTFLAGS / rustc codegen flags that change layout or cfg; (4) sysroot and host vs target triple; (5) build-script and proc-macro generated cfg (execution-capable interacts here); (6) workspace membership and package id; (7) cargo config (net, target overrides). Same source under two dependency feature resolutions is a different universe — omitting lock/package-set identity recreates the unsoundness the section exists to prevent. Author knownLimitations admit unverified general knowledge; this finding states the gap concretely.
findings.requiredFix: Expand keyComponents with package-set/lock identity, explicit cfg corpus, sysroot/triple, and rustc flags hash; or state a deliberately incomplete universe with Coverage reason COVERAGE.LANGUAGE_TIER_UNSUPPORTED / PROVIDER_LIMITATION when any omitted dimension is non-default. Do not seal RESOLVED-INPUTS until P-4a substrate choice makes the key checkable against a real toolchain.
findings.evidenceGrade: toolchain-domain knowledge; not measured on a corpus

findings.title: decisionDependencies cite superseded threat-model.v1 finding IDs
findings.detail: TM.F2 path-traversal and TM.F8 credential handles point at artifacts/threat-model.v1.json. v2 renumbered and re-centered; F8 has no v2 home (see A1-TM2-01). An artifact that claims to discharge TM.F8 while the live model dropped it is paper compliance.
findings.requiredFix: Retarget to v2 findings (V3 path allowlist/symlink; new or restored credential finding). Until F8-class obligation exists in v2, CFG-6 is unrooted in the binding threat model.

findings.title: Layer 2 user-global must split analysis-affecting from non-analysis prefs
findings.detail: Including all user-global settings in PlanId makes results machine-dependent by identity (author correctly prefers visible over portable). But bundling UI/theme/tty prefs with analysis floors creates needless PlanId churn and false cache misses. The peerReview question is right; the fix is not binary include/exclude — it is a declared allowlist of analysis-affecting global keys (mirroring CFG-1 for env).
findings.requiredFix: CFG-style allowlist for user-global keys that affect PlanId; all other global keys forbidden from analysis resolution.

findings.title: Untracked local override that can change verdict is a governance footgun
findings.detail: Layer 4 in PlanId + projection visibility is better than silent. For a guardrail product, an unreviewed file that flips CI when present is still a trust problem (laptop passes, CI fails or vice versa). Alternatives: forbid analysis-affecting untracked overrides; or allow only additive diagnostics, never severity/gate floors.
findings.requiredFix: Product disposition: either ban analysis-affecting untracked overrides, or require a loud Run projection field and CI mode that ignores layer 4.

findings.title: TypeScript semantic universe under-specified relative to Rust attention
findings.detail: P-4 commits two deep providers. Artifact stresses Rust features (correct) but TS universe (tsconfig project references, path maps, module resolution, jsx, lib, paths, solution-style roots, skipLibCheck effects on types) is only 'configuration root set' + generic components. Incomplete TS identity is the same unsoundness class.
findings.requiredFix: Parallel TS keyComponents note: tsconfig graph hash, compilerOptions subset affecting resolution/types, and program root list.

findings.title: No field-level schema — acknowledged; blocks implementability of RI-01/03
findings.detail: knownLimitations already say this. Conformance tests name behaviours that need a schema to fail closed on unknown keys. Acceptable for v1 if seal blocked.
findings.requiredFix: Seal blocker remains until a minimal authored-intent schema exists.

positiveObservations: Precedence order is merited (defaults < global < tracked < untracked < env < flags).
CFG-2 fail-closed unknown keys in tracked intent is correct for a guardrail tool.
CFG-5 per-field provenance into PlanId is the right audit product.
Changed-mode UNAVAILABLE rather than silent full-scope is excellent (avoids false pass).
Impact expansion never under-approximates (RI-11) matches product thesis.
Path canonicalisation + no out-of-root symlink follow aligns with V3.
Author correctly flags Rust unverified and user-global PlanId as arguable — not oversold.
